transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Nayar (Solaris Head of Partnerships), Tom Buckley (Solaris Enterprise Sales Director), Liu Wei (Solaris Solutions Architect), Aisha Rahman (Solaris Channel Manager)

Summary:
Quick co-sell pipeline review and orchestration: align on top 6 accounts for Q4 push, discuss routing of motions (who owns intro/demo/POC), review potential conflicts with other partners and RivalAI, agree on a short benchmark for ACME Inc. and next steps for joint deck and SFDC tags.

Topics:
- Account prioritization and mapping
- Ownership and handoff process
- Joint plays and collateral
- Technical gating and POC requirements
- Competitor positioning

Action items: see metadata action_items field above

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate it. quick around the room, uh, two of us from redwood and the solaris folks? 
[00:07] Priya Nayar: hi, priya here, aisha and tom are with me, and liu is on for the technical piece, thanks for doing this maya
[00:12] Maya Chen: awesome, uh dan and ravi and i will keep this tight, we have about fifty two minutes, aim to leave ten for next steps
[00:21] Daniel Ortiz: yeah and i'll kick in on the infra and benchmarks later, quick high level — we want to coordinate who leads demo vs who follows up on POC
[00:31] Tom Buckley: quick question — last time with RivalAI they promised deeper integrations, are we positioning redwood as lower cost / easier ops or higher perf mostly
[00:41] Maya Chen: good q, we usually frame it as predictable production inference — cost controls + routing + private options. in short: ops and economics for growth, and we have strong perf profiles too
[00:52] Liu Wei: um, from a technical lens, we need to understand KV cache behavior, batch sizing and if your dedicated will support our 8k sequences, that's a blocker for some of our finserv accounts
[01:05] Daniel Ortiz: great callout — we have quantized variants and dedicated pools that handle longer seqs; i'll share a short doc. the dedicated vs hosted decision will hinge on latency SLOs and data residency for those accounts
[01:18] Aisha Rahman: also need SSO and SAML and audit logs for compliance packages — some of the accounts require SOC2 and an audit trail
[01:26] Ravi Patel: noted, we have SOC2 type II and an enterprise compliance pack, we can share the security brief
[01:33] Priya Nayar: what i'm trying to get to here is operational: who owns the first customer intro? solaris wants to keep the relationship, but we want redwood SE to lead the POC technical calls, AE cadence can be joint
[01:44] Maya Chen: makes sense. typical play: partner owns initial intro and relationship, redwood AE runs commercial convo, SE owns POC. we can be flexible regionally
[01:55] Tom Buckley: ok, for account ACME Inc we actually own the exec sponsor — we want redwood to run a quick perf/cost bench and then co-present to the execs
[02:06] Daniel Ortiz: that's doable — can we get a sample dataset and expected workload? even a token distribution and seq length helps
[02:14] Tom Buckley: i'll have liu and a contact send sample prompts, may be noisy but it's a start
[02:18] Liu Wei: yes we'll drop a redacted sample, and note they use long-form transcripts more often
[02:23] Maya Chen: perfect. ok let's walk the pipeline: priya, can you call out the top six targets you want prioritized for joint motions
[02:31] Priya Nayar: sure — ACME Inc, NorthStar Utilities, Meridian Health, Atlas Healthcare(not atlasgrid), BlueRay Logistics, and Orion Financial. those last two are mid-market but high value
[02:44] Daniel Ortiz: quick triage, which of those require data residency or on-prem options? that's a gating Q
[02:51] Priya Nayar: Meridian Health and Orion Financial want strict residency and HSM/KMS, Meridian may require air-gapped for certain pilots
[03:01] Ravi Patel: ok we'll flag those as private deployment prospects; need an internal eligibility checklist, dan will own the feasibility note
[03:10] Daniel Ortiz: yup i'll draft feasibility including estimated cost delta between hosted vs private and rough infra sizes
[03:17] Tom Buckley: competition risk — RivalAI and CloudServe are active on Meridian Health, they push managed models; we need a crisp canary/demo to show latency and deterministic costs
[03:29] Maya Chen: agree, we'll prepare a short two-slide competitive positioning and a 15-min demo script focused on latency & cost predictability
[03:37] Priya Nayar: what's the handoff in SFDC? we had duplicates earlier where both partner and vendor created opps and the AC closed with messy split
[03:46] Ravi Patel: we propose a co-sell tag and a partner-owner field; i'll add the exact tag name and example values to the action items
[03:55] Aisha Rahman: and commission splits — we usually shadow the sales motion; priya we need to confirm revenue share but we can pre-approve a standard template
[04:04] Priya Nayar: yes, we'll share template, churn on legal later, hopefully painless
[04:09] Maya Chen: ok practical next: dan will run bench for ACME, sam? (pause) ravi to create SFDC tags, priya to share account contacts
[04:20] Tom Buckley: one more technical — how do you handle KV cache warming for long convo context with many tokens, does it add latency spikes
[04:28] Daniel Ortiz: it can if you naively reload, we do prefix caching and warm up policies; for long sequences we recommend warm-up tokens staged across workers, i'll share a diagram
[04:38] Liu Wei: would love that, our infra team will need the sequence of warm-up calls
[04:42] Maya Chen: excellent. let's also set a short joint customer success play: redwood CSM and solaris AMs do 30/60/90 check-ins for pilot
[04:52] Ravi Patel: i'll own the 30/60/90 template and share it
[04:56] Priya Nayar: timeline wise we want a Q4 exec pitch for ACME, so need bench results by ~Nov 13 and co-presentation prep week of Nov 17
[05:05] Maya Chen: noted — we'll hit those dates. any open risks? 
[05:10] Tom Buckley: risk: procurement times at healthcare are long; maybe need earlier legal intro
[05:15] Maya Chen: ok we'll loop legal early. ravi can you add procurement contact mapping
[05:20] Ravi Patel: yes, will do
[05:24] [10:22] (note timestamp jump to simulate time progression) Daniel Ortiz: quick deep dive — for Meridian, if they require air-gapped, our on-prem package includes an audit log shim and KMS integration but there is a lead time of around 6 weeks for enterprise install
[10:40] Liu Wei: that lead time is ok, but we need to coordinate scheduling with their infra freeze windows
[10:46] Maya Chen: ok we'll do a readiness checklist and proposed schedule
[11:02] [20:05] Tom Buckley: can we get a sample TCO calc? if redwood can show net savings vs RivalAI at scale, that helps us with execs
[20:13] Maya Chen: yes, we have a basic TCO calc; i'll share a spreadsheet and we'll plug ACME numbers. dan, can you surface per-token cost estimates for standard quant/post-quant runs
[20:23] Daniel Ortiz: will do
[20:27] Priya Nayar: also want a co-branded deck for client-facing pitch, short 5 slides
[20:31] Maya Chen: we can make that. ravi will prep a skeleton deck and send for review
[20:36] Ravi Patel: noted, skeleton deck by end of week
[20:40] [35:12] Maya Chen: ok last few items — visibility: we want weekly check-ins as we approach exec pitch, drop a calendar invite for a 30-minute scrub
[35:22] Priya Nayar: weekly works, prefer Tue mornings
[35:26] Maya Chen: tues morning tentatively
[35:29] Aisha Rahman: PSA — for BlueRay Logistics their procurement insists on ISO certifications; we might need more docs
[35:36] Ravi Patel: we'll attach our compliance matrix to the shared folder
[35:40] Tom Buckley: any blockers on commercial terms? we prefer a simple MSA + SOW route
[35:45] Maya Chen: MSA+SOW is fine, legal will prep a template, we'll share redlines early
[35:50] [47:30] Daniel Ortiz: final note on benchmarking methodology — we'll run a 3-hour run on representative prompts, gather latency p95 and cost per 1k tokens and share raw logs, subject to NDA
[47:42] Priya Nayar: NDA is in place, good
[47:46] Maya Chen: perfect. let's wrap with next steps
[47:52] Maya Chen: recap: maya to send co-sell playbook + deck skeleton, dan to run benchmark plan for ACME, ravi to add SFDC tags and skeleton deck, priya to share contacts and prioritized accounts, all to join weekly Tue morning check-ins
[48:08] Tom Buckley: thanks everyone, appreciate the alignment
[48:12] Priya Nayar: thanks, talk soon
[48:15] Maya Chen: thanks all, end
